verdict.rationale: Both drafts have grounding slips. A says the payout gap was closed 'partly by debt' while long-term debt fell 8.6%, and it omits Argentina from the other-income driver. B's errors are worse: it explains the 0.68x current ratio as cash versus total debt, and says the tax rate 'closes' the net-margin gap. A ties Beauty growth to cited innovation-led volume and sets sensible thresholds. B's watch item pointing toward the impairment-driven 8.1% low is poorly calibrated.

Both drafts have one grounding slip. A says cash versus total debt 'leaves' a 0.68x current ratio, a false causal link. B calls 5.1% capex the window's highest intensity, but FY2017 was about 5.2%, and it credits other income to Glad alone. B goes deeper: cited segment drivers, incremental margin, cost-of-revenue share and ROE context. Its watch thresholds are realistic, unlike A's FY2019 8.1% impairment low.
